title: When Mingus's individuality emerged, and a teacher's candid critique
summary: Callender saw Mingus had arrived with Red Norvo and Tal Farlow, but says he and Gerald Wilson saw what he did not know.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Did you feel that Mingus was bringing something special to the instrument early on?
At the time? No. No, at the time, he wasn't. He was just learning how to play it, like all the rest of us.
At what point did you begin to see the individuality developing?
From the time he went with Red Norvo and Tal Farlow, and I saw that Mingus had arrived. He was playing some astounding... Well, he had astounding facility. He

could play fast, and he was big and strong... I said he was big and strong, and consequently he could play very, very fast on the instrument. So Gerald Wilson and some of the others of us who really knew what was happening used to pick him to pieces from time to time, because we really knew what he knew and what he didn't know musically. He'd get away with a lot of things with his speed that, if you analyzed them, you know, it would be just not too great. And I'm not putting him down at all...
I understand. Well, this is an interesting observation from you, his teacher.
Well, this is an observation from me, who knows, and he knew I knew. He could fool a lot of people with a lot of things, but those of us who really knew what was happening he could not fool.
Did you or Gerald ever say anything to him?
